question.value: To observationally characterize the level of gas ionization at small envelope radii (<= 1000 au) and investigate its relation to the efficiency of magnetic field coupling in the Class 0 protostar B335.

evidence.quote: The purpose of this work is to observationally characterize the level of ionization of the gas at small envelope radii and to investigate its relation to the efficiency of the coupling between the star-forming gas and the magnetic field in the Class 0 protostar B335.

findings_qualitative.value: Deuteration fraction R_D decreases toward the center of B335 (<1%), coinciding with a lack of N2D+ (J=3-2) emission, indicating local destruction of both O-bearing and N-bearing deuterated species near the protostar.

evidence.quote: Indeed, $R_{\rm D}$ decreases down to $<1$% toward the center and the northern region of the source.

A lack of N$_{2}$D$^{+}$ is observed in regions where $R_{\rm D}$ is lower, suggesting that the physical processes lowering the abundance of O-bearing deuterated molecules also lower the abundance of N-bearing deuterated species around the protostar.

findings_qualitative.value: Enhanced gas ionization (chi_e ~ 1-8 x 10^-6) and high cosmic-ray ionization rates (zeta_CR up to ~10^-14 s^-1) in the inner envelope are produced by cosmic rays locally accelerated in shocks near the protostar rather than interstellar Galactic cosmic rays or UV/X-ray photons.

evidence.quote: Our observations suggest that local acceleration of cosmic rays, and not the penetration of interstellar Galactic cosmic rays, may be responsible for the gas ionization in the inner envelope, potentially down to disk-forming scales.

findings_qualitative.value: The high ionization fraction implies strong coupling between the gas and magnetic field (quasi-ideal MHD conditions) in the inner envelope, supporting efficient magnetic braking and explaining the small (<10 au) disk size in B335.

evidence.loc: Magnetic field coupling and non-ideal MHD effects
evidence.quote: The large fraction of ionized gas unveiled by our observations in the inner envelope of B335 should lead to almost perfect coupling of the gas to the local magnetic field lines, generating a drastic braking of rotational motions.

claims.hypothesis: The inner envelope of the Class 0 protostar B335 has a high gas ionization fraction that efficiently couples the gas to the magnetic field, enabling strong magnetic braking.
claims.experiment: Mapped DCO+ (3-2), H13CO+ (3-2), H13CO+ (1-0), C17O (1-0), and 110 GHz dust continuum with ALMA, fitted two velocity components, and applied the Caselli et al. (1998) chemical relations to derive maps of R_D, f_D, chi_e, and zeta_CR at radii <= 1000 au.
claims.result: Measured large ionization fractions chi_e = 1-8 x 10^-6 (mean 2 x 10^-6), which are 1 to 2 orders of magnitude higher than standard density-dependent predictions (10^-7 to 10^-8).
claims.finding: The high ionization fraction leads to strong coupling between the gas and magnetic field in the inner envelope of B335, supporting quasi-ideal MHD conditions and efficient magnetic braking.

evidence.quote: We find large fractions of ionized gas, $\chi_{\rm e}$ $\simeq 1-8 \times 10^{-6}$.
The large fraction of ionized gas we find suggests an efficient coupling between the magnetic field and the gas in the inner envelope of B335.

claims.hypothesis: The enhanced ionization rate in the inner envelope of B335 is driven by locally accelerated cosmic rays rather than interstellar Galactic cosmic rays or protostellar FUV/X-ray radiation.
claims.experiment: Derived the spatial distribution and radial profile of the ionization rate zeta_CR from 40 to 700 au and compared it against FUV attenuation depths, T Tauri X-ray ionization models, and cosmic-ray propagation models.
claims.result: Found zeta_CR increasing toward the protostar up to 7 x 10^-14 s^-1 with a radial power-law slope s = -0.96 +/- 0.04 at r < 270 au, exceeding modelled X-ray ionization rates and Galactic CR levels.
claims.finding: Local acceleration of cosmic rays in jet or accretion shocks near the protostar is responsible for the enhanced gas ionization in the inner envelope.

evidence.loc: Derivation of the CR ionization rate
evidence.quote: At small radii, $r<270$ au, the slope of the power law, $s = -0.96 \pm 0.04$, is compatible with the diffusive regime of CR propagation.
It is evident that X-ray ionization cannot explain the values of the ionization rate estimated from observations.
In particular, we are most likely witnessing the local acceleration of CRs in shocks located in B335 as predicted by theoretical models (cite: Padovani2015; Padovani2016; Padovani2020).

claims.hypothesis: CO is depleted in the inner envelope (<1000 au) of B335 despite expected warm temperatures.
claims.experiment: Computed the ratio of expected CO column density (from 110 GHz dust continuum) to observed CO column density (from C17O J=1-0 emission) across the inner envelope.
claims.result: Found CO depletion factors f_D ranging from 20 to 40 at radii of 1000 to 100 au, increasing up to ~70-80 at the central position.
claims.finding: High CO depletion persists at radii < 1000 au, potentially due to chemical conversion of CO into CH3OH/CH4 or HCO+ promoted by cosmic rays, UV photodissociation, or large dust grains.

evidence.loc: High values of C and O depletion in the source
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 3, we find $f_{\rm D}$ ranging from 20 to 40 at radii of 1000 to 100 au, except at the core center where it increases up to 80.

evidence.loc: High values of C and O depletion in the source
evidence.quote: The high depletion values found at the protostar position are highly uncertain due to unknown optical depth, and unconstrained dust and gas temperatures. We stress that the possible depletion increase toward the center in B335 should be confirmed with further observations of higher J transitions of CO.

why_this_data.value: B335 is an isolated, nearby (164.5 pc) Class 0 protostar with an hourglass magnetic field and no detected disk down to ~10 au; combining multiple ALMA configurations recovers the largest scale range, and the chosen molecular ions/isotopologues constrain R_D, R_H, f_D, chi_e, and zeta_CR.

evidence.quote: Its isolation and relative proximity makes B335 an ideal object with which to test models of star formation.
We used DCO$^{+}$ (J=3-2) and H$^{13}$CO$^+$ (J=3-2) to obtain $R_{\rm D}$ and $\chi_{\rm e}$. We used H$^{13}$CO$^+$ (J=1-0) and C$^{17}$O (J=1-0) to derive the hydrogenation fraction, $R_{\rm H}$.

why_this_method.value: Two velocity components were fitted with HfS because all lines exhibit asymmetric double-peaked profiles tracing distinct gas motions; the Caselli et al. (1998) analytical chemical network is valid in warm (T >= 24 K), dense (n_H ~ 10^6 cm^-3), highly ionized (chi_e >= 3e-7) gas where ortho-to-para H2 variations stabilize.

evidence.quote: As all the molecules present a double-peaked profile with similar velocity patterns to the ones observed in (cite: Cabedo2021b), namely two different velocity components with varying intensity across the source spatial extent, we use two independent velocity components to fit the line profiles simultaneously.

This was also pointed out by (cite: Bron2021) who show that $R_{\rm D}$ is a robust estimator of $\zeta_{\rm CR}$ when the gas is subject to high ionization fractions ($\chi_{\rm e}$$\gtrsim 3 \times 10^{-7}$).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single spherically symmetric infall / self-absorption origin for double-peaked profiles: rejected because optically thin lines (like DCO+ and C17O) show the same two spatially separated velocity components.

evidence.quote: but stress that the small optical depth values found in DCO$^{+}$ confirm that the two velocity components are not mainly produced by self-absorption effects.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Outflow origin for the double-peaked velocity components: rejected because tracer morphologies do not follow the outflow cavity and spectra lack broad high-velocity wings (except for a localized third component in H13CO+ 3-2).

evidence.quote: As none of the tracers present a morphology typical of the outflow cavity, we assume that they are not tracing outflowing gas and that the two velocity components are not caused by this effect.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Far-UV (FUV) photon ionization: ruled out because FUV photon energy (~13 eV) is below the H2 ionization threshold (15.44 eV) and FUV photons are absorbed within a thin column density layer (~3 x 10^20 cm^-2).

evidence.quote: However, ionization by far-UV (FUV) photons can be ruled out. Indeed, the maximum energy of FUV photons is around 13 eV, thus below the threshold for ionization of molecular hydrogen (15.44 eV).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: X-ray ionization from the central protostar: rejected because modeled X-ray ionization rates (using flaring/typical T Tauri spectra) fall well below the observed ionization rates.

evidence.quote: It is evident that X-ray ionization cannot explain the values of the ionization rate estimated from observations.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Interstellar Galactic cosmic-ray penetration: rejected because Galactic CRs are attenuated at high densities and would produce chi_e of 10^-7 to 10^-8, one to two orders of magnitude lower than observed, and would not increase toward the center.

evidence.quote: However, the range of derived values is much higher than those expected from Galactic CRs (cite: Padovani2022).

limitations_admitted.value: Assumption of a constant temperature (T_ex = T_d = 25 K) across the envelope introduces systematic errors of a factor of 3-5 in N_H2, a factor of 2 in N_CO, and a factor of 2-3 in f_D, especially toward the central peak.

evidence.loc: Estimate of the CO depletion in B335
evidence.quote: We estimate that the systematic error is about a factor of 3 to 5, being higher toward the peak position where standard dust properties and conditions of emission may not be met.

evidence.loc: Estimate of the CO depletion in B335
evidence.quote: The CO column density values are subject to systematic uncertainties due to the adopted gas temperature, as this latter is not well constrained and is expected to vary across the envelope. Altogether, the systematic uncertainty is about a factor of 2

limitations_admitted.value: Presence of a third velocity component (outflow contamination) in the southeastern region of H13CO+ (J=3-2) causes poor two-component fits and large errors in R_D there.

evidence.quote: However, these values have the largest associated errors due to the presence of a third velocity component in the line profiles of H$^{13}$CO$^+$ (J=3-2) and should not be totally trusted (see Appendix 8.1).

limitations_admitted.value: Global uncertainties on zeta_CR are of the same order of magnitude as the derived zeta_CR values.

evidence.loc: Derivation of the CR ionization rate
evidence.quote: Considering the systematic uncertainties on n$_{\rm H_{2}}$, and $R_{\rm H}$ we estimate the global uncertainty on $\zeta_{\rm CR}$ values, and find them to be of the same order of magnitude as the $\zeta_{\rm CR}$ values.

limitations_admitted.value: Limited angular resolution (1.5 arcsec ~ 250 au) means only three or four radial points in the zeta_CR profile are completely independent, preventing exact localization of the CR acceleration shock.

evidence.quote: However, we note that these values are also affected by our limited angular resolution of 1.5 arcsec ($\sim$ 250 au), implying that only three or four points in the plot are completely independent, and that observations at larger angular resolution are needed in order to confirm the observed trend.

limitations_admitted.value: Large optical depths (>1) in the central beam for H13CO+ transitions and unknown dust/gas temperatures make central R_D and f_D values uncertain.

evidence.quote: We acknowledge that these large values can potentially affect our deuteration measurements toward the central beam

limitations_admitted.value: Large-scale interferometric filtering produces negative emission bowls in the center and west regions of DCO+ (J=3-2) and H13CO+ (J=3-2).

evidence.quote: The effect of large-scale filtering cannot be ruled out. This is particularly visible in the DCO$^{+}$ (J=3-2) and H$^{13}$CO$^+$ (J=3-2) where negative emission is observed in the center and west regions of the source.

referee_caveats_inferred: Assuming a constant excitation and dust temperature of 25 K down to the central beam ignores the steep protostellar radial temperature gradient; higher temperatures near the center would increase partition functions and alter column densities, optical depths, and CO depletion factors.
The carbon isotopic ratio f_12/13C is used in the equations for R_D and R_H, but the exact numerical value adopted (e.g., 60 vs 70) is not stated in the text.
Using a constant line-of-sight depth L = 1720 au to convert N_H2 to volume density n_H2 across the entire map underestimates the central volume density if the inner envelope is centrally condensed.

missing_for_reproduction: Adopted numerical value of the 12C/13C abundance ratio f_12/13C
Self-calibration parameters (solution intervals, SNR thresholds) and continuum subtraction channel ranges
tCLEAN deconvolution parameters (stopping threshold, masking, niter)
Observation and calibration details for the archival dataset 2015.1.01188.S
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-150 GB of raw ALMA visibilities across 8 execution blocks in 2016.1.01552.S plus archival data from 2015.1.01188.S; ~1-5 GB of reduced image cubes
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project codes, CASA version, calibrators, imaging weights, uv-ranges/tapering, pixel/beam sizes, velocity integration ranges, spectroscopic constants, and analytical chemical equations are all clearly documented. Minor deductions for omitting the numerical value of f_12/13C, self-calibration/continuum-subtraction details, and specific observation tables for 2015.1.01188.S.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Both ALMA datasets (2016.1.01552.S and 2015.1.01188.S) are public in the ALMA archive, the analytical recipe from line cubes to R_D, f_D, chi_e, and zeta_CR is explicit, and the paper provides clear quantitative answer keys (mean column densities, R_D, f_D, chi_e, zeta_CR, and radial power-law slopes).

methods_papers.why: Chemical network equations used to compute ionization fraction chi_e and cosmic-ray ionization rate zeta_CR from DCO+/HCO+ deuteration and CO depletion
HfS spectral line fitting program used to fit two velocity components and derive uncertainties
Dust mass absorption coefficient kappa_0 at 1.3 mm
T Tauri X-ray spectra models used to calculate the X-ray ionization rate zeta_X

companion_papers.why: Paper I of the series, establishing the hourglass magnetic field morphology and centroid position of B335
Previous study of B335 C17O (J=1-0) kinematics by the same authors, providing the C17O comparison maps, two-velocity-component fitting methodology, and core diameter L = 1720 au
CALYPSO survey analysis providing the dust emissivity beta = 0.76 and dust temperature Td = 25 K for B335
